title: Clear three pre-existing high-severity polynomial-ReDoS CodeQL alerts
description:
Discovered while clearing the CodeQL alert on PR #518 (eshyra-o9bd.19.10).

Three `js/polynomial-redos` alerts, all high security-severity, are open on
main and predate that PR (it touches none of these files):

- packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:258
- packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:353
- packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:440

The CodeQL PR check passes because it gates on alerts a PR introduces, so
these do not block any current branch and were not visible as a failure.

The W8 fix is the worked example of the repair shape: an unanchored `\d+` (or
similar unbounded repetition) scanned over text that is not tightly
controlled costs quadratic work across start positions when the rest of the
pattern never matches. Bounding both repetitions to the real domain
(`\d{1,4}`, a single-character separator class) makes the match linear and
kept the behavior identical.

SCOPE
Assess each of the three sites against its actual input source, bound or
restructure the expression, and add an adversarial long-input regression per
site. If a site's input is genuinely trusted and fixed-size, record that
finding and dismiss the alert with the reason rather than changing code.

NON-GOALS
No change to usage-counter or action-economy semantics; this is a
recognizer-shape repair, not a behavior change.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description's stated cause (supervisor forensics, 2026-09-02).

The description says the alerts 'were not visible as a failure' because the PR
check gates on alerts a PR introduces. That is wrong as history.

What actually happened:
- All three alerts were created 2026-07-11T15:43:04Z by the FIRST CodeQL
  analysis of refs/pull/427/head @ c4bb8ec (PR #427, eshyra-2n1t.7, the commit
  that added normalizeAbilityName / normalizeLegendaryName / the trailing-paren
  strip). results_count=3, on the PR, before any main scan saw them.
- They were re-reported on every later PR #427 head (e9deea17, 1c32a05c), each
  results=3. The 'CodeQL' check on PR #427 is FAILURE to this day.
- PR #427 was merged anyway at 2026-07-11T16:32:06Z (merge commit 9bed1613).
  Every refs/heads/main analysis from 9bed1613 onward reports results=3.
- Nothing blocked the merge because the repo's 'main' ruleset (id 16788697)
  carries only deletion, non_fast_forward, and pull_request rules
  (allowed_merge_methods=[merge], required_approving_review_count=0). There is
  NO required_status_checks rule and no bypass actors, so a red CodeQL check —
  or a red build-test — is advisory only. PR #427 is the only merged PR in the
  #427-#430 window with a red CodeQL check.

The description IS right about why they have stayed invisible since: CodeQL
default setup (state=configured, query_suite=default, threat_model=remote,
weekly schedule, no codeql.yml in-repo) runs diff-informed analysis on PR
heads, so a PR touching none of these files reports results=0 while every main
scan reports results=3. PR #518's scans are results=0 for exactly that reason.

Follow-up worth deciding separately (NOT in this bead's scope): whether to add
a required_status_checks rule to the main ruleset. That is a repo-admin
configuration change, not a code fix, and needs the user's decision.

Attempt 2 (eshyra-e1kt.2) integrated: commit c9396ed merged as b0ff8dd, pushed to PR #523. Clears alert #20 (usageCounters.ts:262, /^-+|-+$/g) which surfaced on the PR once the \([^)]*\) sink was removed from the same tainted flow. Independent verify:worktree on the merged content: 273 files passed / 4 skipped, 4827 tests passed / 19 skipped. PR body corrected — the original 'Deliberately unchanged' section claimed line 262 stays, which is no longer true. Awaiting the PR's CodeQL re-run.
BLOCKING review finding on PR #523 @ b0ff8ddf: stripTrailingParenthetical is not equivalent to /\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/. It picks the opening paren with lastIndexOf, but the regex is leftmost-match and [^)]* admits '(', so an EARLIER '(' can start the match. Supervisor reproduced independently: 5 of 22 differential inputs mismatch — '(()' (regex '' vs helper '('), 'name ((x)', 'a ((b)', 'x (( )', '  ((a)  '. Root cause is a false lemma in the attempt-1 spec ('leftmost-match forces the ( to be the last ( in the string'), repeated in the helper doc comment and the PR body; the 'nested (a (b) c)' fixture missed it because an interior ')' makes both candidate opens fail, so the two implementations agreed by accident. Correct rule: the open paren is the LEFTMOST '(' after the last ')' strictly before end-1, i.e. indexOf('(', lastClose+1). Not material to real inputs (no SRD/pack ability name carries an unmatched interior '('), but the bead requires exact equivalence and the differential test is the evidence artifact. Repair dispatched as eshyra-e1kt.3.
Attempt 3 (eshyra-e1kt.3) integrated: commit ae98e4e merged as eced03a, pushed to PR #523 (new head eced03a). stripTrailingParenthetical now selects indexOf('(', lastClose+1). Supervisor evidence beyond the fixture list: exhaustive differential over every string of length <=7 from the alphabet '(' ')' 'a' ' ' — 21845 inputs, 0 mismatches for BOTH stripTrailingParenthetical and replaceParentheticals against their original regexes. Independent verify:worktree on merged content: 273 files passed / 4 skipped, 4827 tests passed / 19 skipped. PR body corrected: the false 'last ( in the string' lemma is replaced with the actual rule and the defect is recorded there.
PR #523 MERGED 2026-09-03T00:51:21Z as merge commit dded2d4 on main. All four reviewed commits reachable from main (2cd2847, c9396ed, ae98e4e, eced03a) — verified with git merge-base --is-ancestor, per the merge-commit ancestry policy. Branch eshyra-e1kt deleted locally and on origin; worktree removed; dispatch .prompt/.pgid cleared (logs kept as evidence). Alerts #15/#16/#17/#20 all cleared; final CodeQL on eced03a reported results=0.
